newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS - Belgian BACOB Bank full of ambition.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Belgian BACOB Bank full of ambition.

text.p: BACOB Bank, Belgium's seventh-largest bank, on Friday announced a takeover, a partnership and an appetite for more.
"We have to grow, the world around us is moving too," BACOB chief executive officer Dirk Bruneel told a news conference about 1996 earnings.

BACOB's 1996 group net profit jumped 40 percent to 2.97 billion francs ($86 million). Total assets rose 28 percent to 1,524 billion ($44 billion) francs, partly because of the first-time consolidation of its 33 percent stake in Credit Agricole/Landbouwkrediet, a small Belgian agricultural bank which it acquired in August 1996.
Bruneel said BACOB wants to grow both in Belgium and abroad and announced two deals to underline that ambition.
He said BACOB had agreed to buy a 75 percent stake in Belgian brokerage Smeets, Verbaet, which employs about 50 people. BACOB employs 3,600 people.
"The aim of this acquisition is to reinforce our capacity with institutional clients and become more active in the share market," Bruneel said. No financial details were given.
The other 25 percent was bought by Dutch Delta Lloyd bank, a unit of Dutch Delta Lloyd Insurance, itself a unit of British Commercial Union.
BACOB also announced it had signed a cooperation agreement with National Bank of Canada (NBC).
The two banks will act as service centers for each others' customers in their own countries, will cooperate on capital markets and have agreed to exchange financial know-how.
Bruneel said NBC was active in 20 states in the United States where it sells mortgage loans. BACOB specialises in the securitisation of mortgage loans.
"We can combine their origination capacity with our securitisation capacity," he said.
He also reiterated that BACOB was still on the lookout for a foreign partner and said for the first time his bank wanted to make more acquisitions in Belgium.
Bruneel said domestic acquisitions would be judged by three criteria -- whether they bring new customers, strengthen BACOB's distribution network and/or contribute specialised knowledge.
"We have 12 to 15 billion francs available for further acquisitions but do not feel limited by this amount," he said.
Bruneel said that BACOB wants to remain a full player in the Belgian domestic market, and that in that respect it was focussing on a geographical niche.

A second target area for growth is financial markets, where BACOB wants to focus on niches, including securitisation and repos. "As the number seven bank in this country (in terms of total assets), we are number one or two in many segments of the capital markets," he said.
In February Bruneel said BACOB was looking for a foreign partner focussing its search on France, Germany, the Netherlands and Austria.
BACOB, an unlisted cooperative bank, is 65.6 percent held by Arcofin, a holding company controlled by the christian- democratic workers movement's Arco group. $1 = 34.6 Belgian francs
